transcript:
Priya: Okay, let's start with the checkout redesign. Where are we?
Marcus: Designs are done. Dev work hasn't started because we're waiting on the API changes.
Priya: Tomás, how are the API changes coming?
Tomás: Mostly done. I still need to write the docs. I'll finish those by Thursday.
Priya: Good. Marcus, can you share the final designs with QA?
Marcus: Already did that last week. But I'll send the updated colour palette to Aiko on Monday.
Aiko: Thanks. I also want to add accessibility tests. I'll draft the test plan by next Friday.
Priya: Great. On a separate note, the analytics dashboard is slow.
Tomás: Yeah, that's a known issue. We should probably look at it at some point.
Priya: Let's not schedule anything yet. Moving on. The offsite budget?
Marcus: Finance still hasn't answered.
Priya: I'll chase them tomorrow.
Aiko: Anything else? No? Okay, bye all.

Helen: Three candidates for the data analyst role. Jamal, did you finish the screening calls?
Jamal: Two of three. The third candidate rescheduled to Wednesday, so I'll call her then and write up notes on Thursday.
Helen: Fine. Sunita, did the take-home test go out?
Sunita: Yes, it went out on Monday.
Helen: Good. Who is checking references for the first candidate?
Sunita: I can do that by the 20th.
Helen: Perfect.
Jamal: One more thing, the job posting still lists the old salary range.
Helen: Oh, right. I'll talk to HR about it.
Sunita: Should we also post it on the university board?
Helen: Maybe. Let's see what the response is first.

Rhea: Post-mortem for last night's outage. Dmitri, what happened?
Dmitri: A config change was pushed without review. The database failover didn't trigger.
Rhea: So two problems. Process and tooling. Lars, can you own the process fix?
Lars: Yes. I'll write a proposal for mandatory config reviews by the end of the week.
Rhea: And tooling?
Dmitri: I'll look into the failover alerts. I should have an answer by Tuesday.
Rhea: Okay. Also, customers were never notified.
Lars: Support said they sent an email at 9 a.m.
Rhea: Good, then that's covered. Chloe, can you pull the incident timeline together for the report?
Chloe: I'm slammed this week. Can it wait until after the holiday?
Rhea: Fine. Do it after the holiday then.
Chloe: Okay.

Nadia: Conference prep. Venue first.
Ethan: The hotel confirmed 120 seats. They need a deposit.
Nadia: Who handles the deposit?
Ethan: Me. I'll pay it on Friday.
Nadia: Great. Speakers?
Olivia: Two have confirmed, three are pending. I'll email the pending ones tomorrow.
Nadia: Perfect. And catering?
Ethan: Last year's caterer was fine.
Nadia: Okay, but nobody has contacted them yet. Olivia, can you add that to your list?
Olivia: Sure, by Wednesday.
Nadia: Lastly, I'll send the draft schedule to everyone before the next meeting.
Ethan: Will there be a registration page?
Nadia: Yes, the web team is building it. Not our problem.

Karim: Let's go around. Lina, your experiments?
Lina: Batch two finished. The results look noisy. I'll rerun the three worst samples tomorrow.
Karim: Good. Wen, your literature review?
Wen: Halfway. I'll send you a draft by the 30th.
Karim: Okay. Lina, also, someone needs to order the reagents.
Lina: I ordered them yesterday.
Karim: Oh good. Then the freezer. It's making that noise again.
Wen: I'll file a maintenance ticket right after this meeting.
Karim: Thanks. I'll submit the conference abstract on the 25th.
Lina: Don't forget the poster.
Karim: Right. That's mine too, but not due until next month.

Sofia: Campaign numbers are in. Clicks up twelve percent.
Brian: Nice. Conversion is flat though.
Sofia: Yes. The landing page hasn't changed since August.
Brian: We talked about redesigning it.
Sofia: We did, but the designer is on leave until January.
Brian: So nothing until then.
Sofia: Right. Budget for Q1?
Brian: Finance says it's unchanged.
Sofia: Good. Newsletter open rates?
Brian: Thirty-one percent, which is above target.
Sofia: Great. I think we're done.
Brian: Oh wait, I'll send you the full report on Friday.
Sofia: Thanks.

Joel: Quarterly review. Everyone's numbers are in the sheet.
Mina: Sales were up, support tickets down.
Joel: Any blockers?
Mina: None that I know of.
Pavel: The migration finished last week, no issues.
Joel: Great. Any risks for next quarter?
Pavel: Hiring is a risk, but that's already being handled by HR.
Mina: Agreed.
Joel: Alright. Thanks everyone, good quarter.

Dalia: Handover meeting for the website project. Karl, you're leaving on the 15th.
Karl: Right. I'll document the deployment steps by the 10th.
Dalia: Good. Who takes over the hosting account?
Karl: Mei does. I'll transfer the credentials to her on the 15th.
Mei: Fine. I'll also rotate the passwords.
Dalia: And the domain renewal?
Karl: It renews automatically in March, no action needed.
Dalia: Perfect. Mei, can you shadow Karl this week?
Mei: Sure, starting tomorrow.
Dalia: Great, thanks both.

Ravi: Who's picking up the client's feedback?
Kate: Sam is out today but he said he'd collect it tomorrow.
Ravi: Great.

Dana: The invoice is overdue.
Liam: Mia knows about it. She's going to call the client on Monday.
Dana: And Noor?
Liam: He is handling the refund. It should be done by Wednesday.

Ines: Our new hire starts next week.
Tobias: I'll set up her laptop on Friday.
Ines: And her accounts?
Tobias: Leo does those. He usually takes a day, so he'll start Thursday.

Gwen: The finance lead will approve it.
Omar: Who is that again?
Gwen: Francesca. She promised to sign off by the 12th.

Yara: Can the two of you finish the slides?
Ben: Sure, Cleo and I will split it. I'll take the first half by Tuesday.
Cleo: And I'll do the second half by Wednesday.

Zane: Dev, could you review my pull request?
Dev: Sure.
Zane: Today if possible.
Dev: Okay, I'll get to it before lunch.

Maya: Theo, you're sending the report on Friday, right?
Theo: Actually the data isn't ready. Can we push it to Monday?
Maya: Yes, Monday is fine.

Ola: Ken will book the flights.
Ken: I can't, my card's expired. Priya, can you?
Priya: Sure, I'll book them tomorrow.

Jin: I'll present the results on Tuesday.
Rosa: The room's taken Tuesday. How about Thursday?
Jin: Thursday works.
Rosa: Okay, I'll reserve the room.

Abel: Ines, please order the swag.
Ines: Okay, I'll order it by the 5th.
Abel: Wait, the budget was cut. Never mind, no swag this year.
Ines: Understood.

Nell: I'll write the summary by Friday.
Owen: You're already swamped. I'll write it instead.
Nell: Thanks, that helps.
Owen: It'll be ready by Friday.

Pia: Can you send the quote today?
Raul: Today is tight. How about tomorrow?
Pia: Tomorrow works.

Ann: Anna, can you update the contract?
Anna: Yes, I'll do that by Wednesday.
Ann: And I'll email it to the client on Thursday.

Chris: Christine, did you get the keys?
Christine: I did. I'll hand them to Chris on Friday.
Chris: Great. I'll unlock the office on Monday morning.

Eli: Elias said he'd fix the build.
Elena: When?
Eli: Tonight. And Elena, can you review it?
Elena: Sure, tomorrow.

Kofi: If the client approves the quote, I'll start the build.
Lara: They haven't replied yet.
Kofi: Then nothing to do for now.

Kofi: If the client approves the quote, I'll start the build on Monday.
Lara: They just approved it. I got the email.
Kofi: Great, then Monday it is.

Tara: Would anyone be able to write the blog post?
Vik: I might be able to, but I'm not sure about my schedule.
Tara: Okay, let me know.

Leah: Did the invoice go out?
Sam: Yes, I sent it this morning, and I'll send the receipt next week.
Leah: Thanks.

Bo: We should really clean the shared drive.
Ida: Yes, it's a mess.
Bo: I'd say it's a nice-to-have.
Ida: Agreed, let's skip it.

Rami: Don't send the report yet. We need legal to review it first.
Joy: Understood, I won't send anything until then.
Rami: I'll ping legal today.

Ursula: Who updated the wiki?
Matt: Dana did, last Friday.
Ursula: Okay good.

Ivan: The demo is on Wednesday.
Hana: Then I'll finish the slides before the demo.
Ivan: And I'll clean up the test data after the demo.

Gus: Payroll runs on the 28th.
Tia: So I'll submit the timesheets by the 25th.
Gus: And I'll approve them on the 26th.

Elsa: The launch is in two weeks.
Finn: Then I'll freeze the code in one week.
Elsa: Good. I'll write the press release in ten days.

Cara: End of the month is tight.
Dev: I'll close the books by the last day of the month.
Cara: And I'll reconcile the accounts at the end of Q3.

Mo: Do you have a deadline in mind?
Eva: The board meets on March 12.
Mo: Then I'll have the draft ready by March 5.
Eva: And I'll proofread it on March 9.

Ruth: The vendor promised to deliver on Friday.
Pat: Great, so nothing for us to do.
Ruth: Right.

Ty: The web team will fix it next week.
Uma: Good. Then I'll hold off on the release.
Ty: Sounds right.

Nico: Can anyone cover Saturday?
Ada: I can't, sorry.
Bea: Me neither.
Nico: Okay, never mind then.

Gina: Back to the budget.
Ray: Sorry, quick aside: I'll bring the cake on Friday for Lee's birthday.
Gina: Ha, thanks. Budget: all good?
Ray: Yes.

Ali: I called the printer yesterday. They said Chen should send the files by Monday.
Chen: Okay, I'll do that.
